title: Velvet Ante: building and checking an AI-assisted browser poker roguelike
author: OakHeart123
selftext:
I have been building Velvet Ante, a free browser poker roguelike inspired by Balatro, with AI assistance on the code and procedural audio. The card illustrations are AI-generated too.



The game is about scoring poker hands and finding joker combinations. It has 50 jokers, Tarot/Planet/Spectral upgrades, eight escalating antes, endless play and seeded runs.



For the release, I checked the actual browser experience alongside the automated tests: dealing and discarding, a scoring hand, buying a joker, then reloading to check the purchase and save survived. The automated checks cover gameplay and saves as well as the feedback system. I have inspected a narrow layout, but physical-phone testing and a manual full-campaign win are still open. Passing the rule checks does not tell me whether the balance feels good.



I would like to hear how other people using AI for game development check that gap between working rules and a satisfying run. If you try this one, where does the first run stop being clear, and do the joker choices feel meaningful?



Play free, without a download or account: [https://velvet-ante-joel.starry-hill-5513.chatgpt.site/?utm\_source=community](https://velvet-ante-joel.starry-hill-5513.chatgpt.site/?utm_source=community)



Menu > Leave feedback sends private notes. Progress saves locally in the same browser and device. Not affiliated with Balatro or its creators; no real-money wagering or cash prizes.
